# ML Fundamentals Refresher {#sec-appendix-ml}

::: {.callout-note}
This appendix is a fast-recall reference for concepts that appear in screening rounds and onsite interviews across all experience levels. Detailed treatment of each topic is in the main chapters.
:::

## Core Algorithm Quick Reference

| Algorithm | Loss Function | Output | Regularization | Scale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linear Regression | MSE | Continuous | L1 (Lasso), L2 (Ridge) | Normal equations: O(n·d²); GD: O(n·d) |
| Logistic Regression | Cross-entropy | Probability [0,1] | L1/L2 | O(n·d) per epoch |
| Decision Tree | Gini/Entropy | Class/Value | max_depth, min_samples | O(n·d·log n) |
| Random Forest | Avg of trees | Class/Value | n_estimators, max_features | O(k·n·d·log n) |
| Gradient Boosting | Residual MSE/log-loss | Class/Value | learning_rate, max_depth | O(n·d·T) |
| SVM | Hinge loss | Class | C (margin width) | O(n²–n³) |
| k-NN | — | Majority/mean | k, distance metric | O(n·d) per query |
| K-Means | Inertia (SSE) | Cluster ID | k, max_iter | O(n·k·d·T) |
| PCA | Variance explained | Low-dim projection | n_components | O(n·d²) or randomized O(n·d·k) |
| Naive Bayes | Log-likelihood | Probability | α (Laplace smoothing) | O(n·d) |

## Essential Math Reference

### Linear Algebra

| Symbol/Operation | Meaning | ML Use |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathbf{A}^\top$ | Transpose | Swap rows/cols; $(\mathbf{AB})^\top = \mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{A}^\top$ |
| $\mathbf{A}^{-1}$ | Inverse | Solve $\mathbf{Ax}=\mathbf{b}$: $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{A}^{-1}\mathbf{b}$ |
| $\|\mathbf{x}\|_2$ | L2 norm | $\sqrt{\sum x_i^2}$ — Euclidean distance |
| $\|\mathbf{x}\|_1$ | L1 norm | $\sum \lvert x_i\rvert$ — Manhattan distance; promotes sparsity |
| $\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y}$ | Dot product | $\sum x_i y_i = \|\mathbf{x}\|\|\mathbf{y}\|\cos\theta$ |
| $\cos\theta$ | Cosine similarity | $\frac{\mathbf{x}\cdot\mathbf{y}}{\|\mathbf{x}\|\|\mathbf{y}\|}$ — embedding similarity |
| Eigenvalue $\lambda$ | $\mathbf{Av} = \lambda\mathbf{v}$ | PCA directions; gradient signal |
| SVD | $\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{U\Sigma V}^\top$ | Dimensionality reduction; LoRA |
| Rank | Independent rows/cols | LoRA rank r controls parameter budget |
| Trace | $\sum_i A_{ii}$ | $\text{tr}(\mathbf{AB})=\text{tr}(\mathbf{BA})$ |

### Probability

| Concept | Formula | ML Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| Bayes theorem | $P(A\|B) = \frac{P(B\|A)P(A)}{P(B)}$ | Posterior = likelihood × prior / evidence |
| MLE | $\hat\theta = \arg\max_\theta \prod_i P(x_i\|\theta)$ | Maximizes data likelihood |
| MAP | $\hat\theta = \arg\max_\theta P(\theta)\prod_i P(x_i\|\theta)$ | MLE + prior = regularization |
| KL divergence | $\sum_x p(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ | Asymmetric; RLHF KL penalty, VAE |
| Cross-entropy | $-\sum_x p(x)\log q(x) = H(p) + D_{KL}(p\|q)$ | Classification loss |
| Entropy | $H(X) = -\sum_x p(x)\log p(x)$ | Decision tree splits, information theory |
| Gaussian | $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$: $f(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}$ | Weight init, noise modeling |
| CLT | $\bar X \to \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2/n)$ | Justifies averaging, A/B test stats |
| p-value | $P(\text{data this extreme} \| H_0 \text{ true})$ | Reject $H_0$ if $p < \alpha = 0.05$ |
| Type I/II error | False positive / False negative | $\alpha$ controls Type I; power = 1 - Type II |

### Calculus for ML

| Concept | Formula | ML Use |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient | $\nabla_\theta L$ — vector of partial derivatives | Direction of steepest ascent |
| Chain rule | $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial z}\frac{\partial z}{\partial w}$ | Backpropagation |
| Jacobian | $J_{ij} = \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}$ | Multi-output gradients |
| Hessian | $H_{ij} = \frac{\partial^2 L}{\partial w_i \partial w_j}$ | Second-order optimization |
| Sigmoid derivative | $\sigma'(x) = \sigma(x)(1-\sigma(x))$ | Vanishes for large $\lvert x\rvert$ — saturation |
| ReLU derivative | $\text{ReLU}'(x) = \mathbb{1}[x > 0]$ | Dead neurons if always $x < 0$ |

## Regularization Reference

| Method | Penalty | Effect | Use When |
|---|---|---|---|
| L2 (Ridge, Weight Decay) | $\lambda\|\mathbf{w}\|_2^2$ | Shrinks all weights | Dense features; neural nets (as weight decay) |
| L1 (Lasso) | $\lambda\|\mathbf{w}\|_1$ | Zeros out weights | Sparse features; feature selection |
| Elastic Net | $\alpha\|\mathbf{w}\|_1 + (1-\alpha)\|\mathbf{w}\|_2^2$ | Both effects | High-dim with correlated features |
| Dropout | Random zero at rate $p$ | Ensemble effect | Neural nets; during training only |
| Early Stopping | Stop at min val loss | Implicit regularization | Always — simple and free |
| Data Augmentation | Transform inputs | Reduces variance | Computer vision; text (synonym swap) |
| BatchNorm | Normalize layer activations | Smooths loss landscape | Deep nets (especially CNNs) |
| Label Smoothing | Replace 1/0 with 0.9/0.1 | Reduces overconfidence | Classification with noisy labels |

## Optimizer Reference

| Optimizer | Update Rule | Adaptive LR | Memory Overhead | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SGD | $\theta \leftarrow \theta - \alpha g$ | No | 0 | Simple problems; when Adam diverges |
| Momentum | $v \leftarrow \beta v + g$; $\theta \leftarrow \theta - \alpha v$ | No | 1× params | Smooth loss landscapes |
| AdaGrad | $\theta \leftarrow \theta - \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{G+\epsilon}} g$ | Yes (per-param) | 1× params | Sparse features; embeddings |
| RMSprop | EMA of $g^2$; divide update | Yes | 1× params | RNNs; non-stationary objectives |
| Adam | Momentum + RMSprop | Yes | 2× params | Default for most deep learning |
| AdamW | Adam + explicit weight decay | Yes | 2× params | Transformers (decouples decay from Adam) |

Adam memory: $m_t$ (first moment) + $v_t$ (second moment) = 2× the parameter count in additional optimizer state.

## Model Sizing Formulas

**Parameters from architecture:**
$$\text{Params} \approx 12 \cdot n_{layers} \cdot d_{model}^2$$
(Accounts for: 4 attention weight matrices of $d_{model}^2/4$ each, 2 FFN layers of $4 \cdot d_{model}^2$ each)

**Memory for inference (BF16):**
$$\text{VRAM (GB)} = \frac{\text{Params} \times 2}{10^9}$$
(2 bytes per parameter in BF16)

**Memory for training (full precision + Adam):**
$$\text{VRAM (GB)} = \frac{\text{Params} \times 16}{10^9}$$
(2 for weights + 2 for gradients + 4 for Adam $m_t$ + 4 for Adam $v_t$ + 4 for optimizer fp32 copy)

**KV cache per token per layer:**
$$\text{KV cache per token} = 4 \times d_{model} \times \text{bytes per param}$$
(2 for K, 2 for V; each of size $d_{model}$)

**Quick estimates:**

| Model | Params | BF16 inference | Full train |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7B | 7B | ~14 GB | ~112 GB |
| 13B | 13B | ~26 GB | ~208 GB |
| 70B | 70B | ~140 GB | ~1.1 TB |
| 405B | 405B | ~810 GB | ~6.5 TB |

## Evaluation Metrics Quick Reference

### Classification

| Metric | Formula | Use When |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | (TP+TN)/(P+N) | Balanced classes only |
| Precision | TP/(TP+FP) | False positives are costly (spam filter) |
| Recall | TP/(TP+FN) | False negatives are costly (cancer screening) |
| F1 | 2·P·R/(P+R) | Imbalanced; single metric needed |
| AUC-ROC | Area under ROC curve | Ranking quality; threshold-independent |
| MCC | Correlation between predicted/actual | Best single metric for imbalanced |
| Log loss | $-\frac{1}{n}\sum y_i\log\hat{p}_i$ | Probabilistic predictions |

### Regression

| Metric | Formula | Sensitive To |
|---|---|---|
| MAE | $\frac{1}{n}\sum\lvert y_i - \hat{y}_i\rvert$ | All errors equally |
| MSE | $\frac{1}{n}\sum(y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2$ | Large errors (squared) |
| RMSE | $\sqrt{\text{MSE}}$ | Large errors; same units as target |
| R² | $1 - \frac{SS_{res}}{SS_{tot}}$ | Fraction of variance explained |
| MAPE | $\frac{1}{n}\sum\left\lvert\frac{y_i-\hat{y}_i}{y_i}\right\rvert$ | Relative error (undefined if $y_i=0$) |

### Information Retrieval / RAG

| Metric | Formula | What It Measures |
|---|---|---|
| Precision@k | Relevant in top-k / k | Quality of top-k results |
| Recall@k | Relevant found in k / total relevant | Coverage at k |
| MRR | $\frac{1}{\lvert Q\rvert}\sum_q \frac{1}{\text{rank}_q}$ | Rank of first relevant result |
| NDCG@k | Normalized discounted cumulative gain | Graded relevance with position discount |
| Faithfulness | Is answer grounded in context? | RAG hallucination rate |

## Big-O Complexity Reference

| Operation | Time | Space | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matrix multiply (n×n) | O(n³) | O(n²) | Strassen: O(n^2.37) |
| Self-attention (seq len n) | O(n²·d) | O(n²) | Quadratic in sequence length |
| FlashAttention | O(n²·d) | O(n) | Same FLOPs, IO-efficient |
| KV cache lookup | O(1) | O(n·d) per layer | Per-token at inference |
| HNSW search | O(log n) | O(n) | ANN approximate |
| IVF search | O(√n·d) | O(n) | Exact within clusters |
| Exact k-NN | O(n·d) | O(1) | Brute-force search |
| MinHash dedup | O(n·b) | O(n) | b = num hash bands |

## Activation Functions

| Function | Formula | Range | Use Case | Avoid When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sigmoid | $\frac{1}{1+e^{-x}}$ | (0,1) | Binary output layer | Hidden layers (vanishing gradient) |
| Tanh | $\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}{e^x+e^{-x}}$ | (-1,1) | RNN hidden states | Deep nets (vanishing gradient) |
| ReLU | $\max(0,x)$ | [0,∞) | CNNs, MLPs | Deep nets with poor init (dead neurons) |
| Leaky ReLU | $\max(0.01x, x)$ | (-∞,∞) | When dead ReLUs are a problem | — |
| GELU | $x\cdot\Phi(x)$ | ≈(-0.17,∞) | Transformers (BERT, GPT) | Compute-constrained edge devices |
| SiLU/Swish | $x\cdot\sigma(x)$ | ≈(-0.28,∞) | LLaMA, Mistral FFN | — |
| Softmax | $\frac{e^{x_i}}{\sum_j e^{x_j}}$ | (0,1), sum=1 | Attention, output layer | — |

## GenAI Acronym Reference

| Acronym | Full Form | Key Idea |
|---|---|---|
| LLM | Large Language Model | Autoregressive transformer pretrained on text |
| SFT | Supervised Fine-Tuning | Train on (instruction, response) pairs |
| RLHF | Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback | PPO on human preference reward |
| DPO | Direct Preference Optimization | Implicit reward from preference pairs |
| PPO | Proximal Policy Optimization | RL algorithm with clipped objective |
| GRPO | Group Relative Policy Optimization | Group sampling replaces critic model |
| LoRA | Low-Rank Adaptation | ΔW = BA, small rank matrices |
| QLoRA | Quantized LoRA | NF4 4-bit base + LoRA adapter |
| PEFT | Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning | Umbrella: LoRA, prefix, prompt tuning |
| RAG | Retrieval-Augmented Generation | Retrieve docs → augment prompt → generate |
| KV Cache | Key-Value Cache | Cached attention keys/values for decode |
| GQA | Grouped Query Attention | Multiple query heads share K/V heads |
| MQA | Multi-Query Attention | All query heads share one K/V head |
| MHA | Multi-Head Attention | Original: Q/K/V heads all equal |
| RoPE | Rotary Position Embedding | Positional encoding via rotation |
| ALiBi | Attention with Linear Biases | Position bias in attention score |
| SAE | Sparse Autoencoder | Decomposes activations into sparse features |
| MoE | Mixture of Experts | Sparse activation of expert FFN layers |
| SSM | State Space Model | Recurrent with selective state (Mamba) |
| HNSW | Hierarchical Navigable Small World | ANN graph index for vector search |
| IVF | Inverted File Index | Cluster-based ANN for vector search |
| PQ | Product Quantization | Compress vectors via subspace quantization |
| TTFT | Time to First Token | Latency of prefill phase (user experience) |
| TPOT | Time Per Output Token | Decode latency per generated token |
| TPS | Tokens Per Second | Throughput metric for serving |
| vLLM | Virtual LLM (PagedAttention) | GPU memory manager for KV cache |
| BPE | Byte Pair Encoding | Subword tokenizer via frequency merges |
| CFG | Classifier-Free Guidance | Scale between conditional and unconditional |
| DDPM | Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model | Gaussian noise diffusion training |
| DDIM | Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models | Deterministic, fewer steps |
| MCP | Model Context Protocol | Anthropic's standard for model-tool APIs |
| ReAct | Reason + Act | Interleaved thought-action agent loop |
| TIES | Trim, Elect Sign, Merge | Multi-model merge interference reduction |
| DARE | Drop And REscale | Sparse task vectors for cleaner merges |
| SLERP | Spherical Linear Interpolation | Norm-preserving 2-model merge |

## Interview Q&A: Entry-Level Screening

**Q: What is the bias-variance tradeoff?**

Bias = systematic error from wrong model assumptions (underfitting). Variance = error from sensitivity to training data fluctuations (overfitting). High-bias example: linear regression on a nonlinear problem. High-variance example: decision tree with no depth limit. Increasing complexity reduces bias but raises variance. The goal is the minimum of bias² + variance + irreducible noise.

---

**Q: When use L1 vs L2 regularization?**

L2 (Ridge): shrinks all weights proportionally, rarely to zero. Use for dense feature sets, neural networks (as weight decay). L1 (Lasso): drives weights to exactly zero, producing sparse models. Use for feature selection, high-dimensional sparse data (NLP bag-of-words). Elastic Net combines both when you're uncertain.

---

**Q: Your model has 95% accuracy on a 95/5 class split. Is it good?**

Probably not. A trivial "always predict majority class" baseline achieves 95% accuracy on a 95/5 split. Check: precision = 0, recall = 0, F1 = 0 for the minority class. Use AUC-ROC, F1, or MCC to evaluate imbalanced classifiers, not raw accuracy.

---

**Q: What is cross-validation and when do you use it?**

k-fold CV trains on k-1 folds, validates on 1, rotates k times, reports average. Use when: dataset is small (reduces variance of performance estimate), hyperparameter tuning (prevents test set leakage), or when you need confidence intervals on performance. Computationally expensive: k=5 means 5× training runs. For large datasets, a single holdout split is often sufficient.

---

**Q: How does gradient descent work?**

Compute gradient of loss with respect to all parameters (backpropagation). Step in the negative gradient direction: θ ← θ - α·∇L. Repeat until convergence. Mini-batch SGD (batches of 32–256) is the standard variant. Adam extends this with adaptive per-parameter learning rates based on first and second moment estimates of the gradient.
